thread:
incident-bot: Pager — CPU OOM detected on tokenizer-prep deployment in prod-us-west-2. 6 pods evicted within 2m. Alerts: cpu_util=99%, kernel OOM, eviction events.

maria: I'm on it. Grafana shows correlated CPU spikes on node gke-token-3 and gke-token-4. Pod logs: repeated "fatal: allocator out of memory" from tokenizer preproc worker.

ajay: grabbing k8s state and logs. running: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=tokenizer-prep -o wide` and `kubectl -n prod describe pod tokenizer-prep-5f7d`

leo: routing change ready. Will shift tokenization traffic to fallback-model and apply temporary global rate-limit on /v1/generate to reduce burst pressure.

maria: mitigation steps I'm running now:
```
kubectl -n prod cordon gke-token-3
kubectl -n prod drain gke-token-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
kubectl -n prod scale deployment/tokenizer-prep --replicas=3
```

tina: applied WAF rule wg-429 to throttle large prompt bursts from the internal gateway. Also updating ConfigMap: `tokenizer.max_concurrency: 8 -> 2` as emergency throttle.

ajay: logs snippet from tokenizer-prep-5f7d:
```
[2026-03-15T12:05:23Z] ERROR oom: failed allocate 5242880 bytes
[2026-03-15T12:05:23Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (python) score 987
```

maria: confirm: this is CPU/host OOM. No CUDA trace, GPUs fine. Hypothesis: extremely large prompts or pathological tokenization regex backtracking causing runaway CPU and memory usage.

infra-sre: node memory pressure triggered kubelet eviction. Node had 6 tokenizer pods + some adhoc batch workers. Suggest cordon + move batch jobs to standby nodes, and scale up node pool temporarily.

ajay: will prepare a hotfix: add early bailout for prompts > 120k chars and reduce backtracking in tokenization regex. Also bump container ulimits as guard. Pushing a patch now.

deploy-bot: CI green for hotfix branch `hotfix/tokenizer-preproc-oom`. Deploying canary (1 pod) to prod-us-west-2.

maria: canary up. Observing CPU. Canary CPU ~55% and stable; no OOM so far.

leo: routing update: directing 30% traffic to canary, remaining to fallback-model. Keeping overall ingress rate capped at 60rps per shard.

cs-rep: impact: customers experienced some 502s and timeouts between 12:04–12:18. Currently ~12 customer tickets flagged as P2. Preparing customer comms.

tina: scaled node pool +2 nodes to drain backlog and prevent further evictions. Also restarted some long-running batch jobs on separate nodes.

maria: after 12:22 CPU stabilized cluster-wide, no new OOM evictions seen. Restarted drained node after moving workloads.

ajay: merged patch to main: tokenizer bailout + regex fixes. Will open follow-up eval to detect similar worst-case prompts in the future and add a pre-filter in the API gateway.

maria: handing off active watch to ops-rotation for overnight monitoring. Mitigations applied: canary healthy, rate-limits in place, node pool scaled. Handoff note: monitor tokenization_oom_rate and pod_eviction_count.

ops-rotation: ack, taking over at 12:40. Adding watch alert: `tokenization_oom_rate > 0.5% for 30m` and `pod_eviction_count > 1 in 10m` to escalation.

maria: creating incident record INC-2026-137 and assigning to ajay + infra-sre for postmortem. Initial RCA: lack of defensive limits in tokenizer for extreme prompt lengths combined with colocated batch jobs on nodes.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=P2, customer-impact=partial, status=mitigated. Pages cleared.

cs-rep: customer comms draft: "We experienced a brief service disruption affecting generation requests. Our team deployed mitigations and a patch; normal service has resumed. We are doing a postmortem and will follow up with details."

ops-rotation: will keep monitoring for 4 hours and escalate if OOMs reappear. Closing active page for now. :thumbsup:
